2. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner Meher Ali is that he instituted Title Suit No. 56/84 in the court of Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj against the defendant opposite parties A.K. Murshed, Full Chand Mia, Rahatan, Milan Mia, Razzak and Aklima praying for a decree of declaration of plaintiffs title in .16 acre of plot No.131 (Shabek Pukurpar-at present bhiti) and .21 acre of .plot No. 132.(Shahck pukurpar-at present bhiti) of mouza Hajiganj, P.S. Narayanganj, District Narayanganj and also for a declaration that defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed is a tenant in the premises in the suit land. Plaintiff and defendant Nos. 2-6 are sub-lessees inducted by defendant No. l. The suit land originally belonged to the Zamindari Estate of Ram Ratan Sharma which was seized, owned and possessed by Suresh Chandra Poddar, Joy Durga Daysa, Govinda Chandra Poddar, Mem Chandra Chowdhury, Nawab Ali Chowdhury and others in odd shares and their names with their shares were correctly recorded in the maliki claim of C.S. Khatian. Nawab Ahsanullah Bahadur represented by Manager, Court of Wards Estates, Dhaka owner of pattani taluk was immediate tenant under the said Zamindars with respect to the suit land. The said Manager, Court of Wards Estate, Dhaka leased out the suit land along with other lands as raiyats in favour of Shorojini Bala Dutta who seized, owned and possessed the suit lands along with other lands as permanent raiyat under the said Court of Wards Estate of Dhaka. Shorojini Bala Dutta constructed tinhuts in the suit land and let out the premises to defendant No.1 as monthly tenant. She executed a Will dated 4.12.82 in favour of her daughter-in-law Anjali Rani Dutta. After the death of Shorojini Bala Dutta her daughter-in-law Anjali Rani Dutta obtained probate of the said Will in Probate Misc. Case No. 103/63 in the 4th Court of Munsif, Narayanganj on 20.5.64 and thus became owner of the suit lands and the premises therein along with other lands of the said Will. Anjali Rani Dutta sold out the suit lands and the premises therein along with other lands to the plaintiff by registered sale deed dated 26.6.89. Defendant No.1 opposite party A.K. Murshed entering into occupation of the premises of the suit land as an ordinary ejectable monthly tenant under Shorojini Bala Dutta, paid monthly rents to her. The defendant No. 1 continued his occupation in the suit lands as usual during the ownership of Anjali Rani Dutta who delivered possession of the suit and the premises to the plaintiff along with the ordinary ejectable occupation of the said monthly tenant defendant No. 1 opposite party A.K. Murshed and thus defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed became tenant under the plaintiff. As defendant No. 1 became defaulter and as he sublet a portion of the premises in the suit land illegally without permission of his land lady to defendant No. 2 Ful Chand Mia and Rustam Ali Mia (predecessor of defendant Nos. 3-6), the plaintiff terminated his tenancy by quit notice dated 16.1.70 with the expiry of the month of February, 1970 directing him to hand over vacant possession of the premises in the suit land with the expiry of tilt month of February, 1970. As defendant No.1 A K. Murshed did not comply with the said quit notice, the plaintiff instituted SCC Suit No. 5/70 in the SCC Court of 4th Munsif, Narayanganj for ejectment of defendant Nos. 1-2 and Rustom Ali Mia, that the said SCC Suit was decreed ex parte on 19.5.72 with cost. Defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed filed Misc. Case No. 77/72 under Order 9, rule 13 C.P.C. for setting aside the said ex parte decree which was allowed on contest on 30.12.72. Thereafter it was found that the said Misc. Case No. 77/72 was filed without depositing the cost or submitting any security as per provision of section 17(1) of SCC Act Hence the plaintiff challenged the validity of the order dated 13.12.72 in the said Misc. Case No. 77/72 in Title Suit No. 182/75 (probably it is a mistake for 1974) as it appears from the judgment of the Appellate Division in the case of Murshed Ahmed Vs. Meher Ali 35 DLR (AD) 178 in the Second Court of Munsif, Narayanganj which was de-creed on contest by judgment dated 31.1.77. Defendant No.1 preferred Title Appeal No. 39/77 in the court of District Judge, Dhaka against the said decree in Title Suit No. 182/75 (1974) which was dismissed on contest by judgment dated 28.12.78. Defendant No. 1 preferred Second Appeal No. 177/78 before this court and a learned Single Judge of this court dismissed the said Second appeal on contest by judgment dated 5.4.82 Thereafter defendant No. 1. filed civil appeal No. 136/82 before the Appellate Division and the same was allowed on contest by judgment dated 27.1.83 which is reported in 35 DLR (AD) 178. The said SCC Suit No. 5/70, the further proceedings of which remained stayed during the said interim period was made ready for trial after vacating the stay order in SCC Court of the 4th Court of Munsif, Narayanganj. Major Monwar Hossain, son of defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed, being an army personnel managed to have said SCC Suit No. 5/70 transferred to Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 at Narayanganj on 25.7.83 by Major General N.A. Chisty illegally by gazette Notification No. 142 dated 25 July 1983 (published in the Bangladesh Gazette on 26th July, 1983). Defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed in the Summary Military Court claimed adverse possession in the suit land without observing the legal requirements of first surrendering the possession of the property to the owner and then regaining the same through court on establishing adverse possession. Defendant No. 1 thus has got no legal right to set up the plea of adverse possession in the suit land. The defendants since 19.4.84 have recently started making open denial of the plaintiffs title in the suit lands. In view of this the cause of action of the present suit has arisen. As the SCC Suit No. 5/70 has not yet been finally disposed of by judgment, the plaintiff has no other alternative but to take shelter of the civil court for appropriate relief. The plain-tiff prayed for leave of the court for consequential relief after getting back the SCC Suit No. 5/70 from the review court of the Zonal Martial Law Court Administrator. The cause of action of the present suit arose on and from 19.4.84 when the defendants openly denied the title of the plaintiff in the suit land and disclosed that they will henceforth deal with the suit lands as owners of the same. 

 3. On 9.5.84 the plaintiff-petitioner Meher Ali filed a petition for amendment of the plaint under rule 17 of Order 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground that the plaint of the suit was drafted hurriedly. Among various minor amendments it was prayed that in paragraph 16 of the present plaint in the 7th line the word 'lands' will be deleted and thereafter the following shall be inserted, "defendant No. 1 became defaulter in payment of rent and as such Shorojini Bala instituted a case in the court of the House Rent Controller, Narayanganj for permission to sue for ejectment of defendant No.1 on the ground of default". In the said case defendant No. 1 was directed to pay the rent with effect from 1.3.50 etc. and the prayer for permission to sue for ejectment of defendant No. 1 was ultimately rejected. The appeal against the said order dismissed on contest asking defendant No. 1 to pay all arrears rents up to May, 1953 or in default of such payment the landlord appellant is permitted to sue the tenant for ejectment on the ground of default, that the Summary Military Court No. 25 in spite of application has not sup-plied the plaintiff with the report regarding the fate of the SCC suit No. 5/70, that defendant No.1 with the help of the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Narayanganj with police force and many unknown people damaged the dochala tin hut, dochala cowshed, and dochala kitchen and two other dochala tin-huts from the suit premises and looted away C.I. sheets etc. and constructed 3 pucca boundary walls in the suit plots. That defendant No. 1 on 21.4.84 has filed a copy of the Gazette Notification No. 142, Dhaka dated 25.7.83 showing the illegal transfer of SCC Suit No. 5/70 from the Second Court of Munsif, Narayanganj to the Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 Dhaka and also filed copy of the illegal order of the Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 to the effect that he (defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed) is not tenant under the plaintiff, that SCC Suit No. 5/70 is dismissed and that the plaintiff and others be evicted from the suit land and that the suit land is distributed to defendant No. 1 A.K. Murshed, one Mir Sayed Ali and the Government of Bangladesh (who are to be added as defendants 7 and 8 respectively in the plaint), that the Summary Martial Law Court No. 25 at Narayanganj was constituted for trial of certain offences and not for adjudication of civil suits involving right to property, that the Summary Martial Law Court had no jurisdiction to try the SCC Suit, that by virtue of order of the summary Military Court in disposing SCC suit illegally the plaintiff cannot be evicted or plaintiffs right, title and interest in the suit property cannot be affected. Nor can the suit property be distributed among defendant Nos. 1, 7 and 8, that the order of the Summary Military Court is void ab initio, without jurisdiction, malafide, baseless and has no legal effect or force and does not bind the plaintiff as the Summary Military Court exercises its power illegally and without jurisdiction and malafide with colourable use of power and without lawful authority and that in paragraph 21(b) it should be added that the prayer for a decree for eviction of the defendants from the suit premises through court demolishing the boundary walls if made during the pendency of the suit. 

 12. Thus it is clear that the Chief Martial Law Administrator who was the sole law making Authority during the continuance of Martial Law at that time was the sole law making authority and although by Martial Law Regulation No. I of 1982 promulgated on March 24, 1982 by Regulation 2(3) of M.L.R. No. I the Chief Martial Law Administrator or an Officer authorised by him in this behalf was empowered to transfer a case from a civil court to Martial Law Court; but the Chief Martial Law Administrator and the Commander-in-Chief by Martial Law Regulation No. III of 1982 amended the same with retrospective effect from 24.3.82 omitting the power to transfer a case from a civil court to a Martial Law Court it may be that even after such amendment the Chief Martial Law Administrator as the sole law making Authority perhaps could have himself transferred the S.C.C.
